description.p: Browse your local files and a remote server side by side, then drag, drop, or double-click to move things between them. Think FileZilla or WinSCP, built fresh in Qt6.

ul.li: Dual-pane browsing with back/forward/up navigation per pane
SFTP with password or private-key login
Site Manager for saved connections, organized into groups
Real trust-on-first-use host-key and certificate verification
Drag-and-drop or multi-select transfers, whole folders included
A real transfer queue: live progress and speed, pause/resume, cancel, retry
Destination conflict handling — always asks before overwriting anything

description.p: This is beta software: real functionality, with real but narrowing gaps — see the Known Limitations section in the project's README before relying on it for anything you can't afford to get wrong. The project is in feature freeze heading toward 1.0: releases from here are bug fixes and small additions, not new capabilities.

screenshot.caption: Dual-pane browsing, connected to a real SFTP server
A real transfer in progress in the Transfers panel

description.p: First beta. The project enters feature freeze from here toward a 1.0 release — bug fixes and small additions closing existing gaps, not new capabilities. A signed, installer-based Windows build is planned at some point during this phase.
Real .deb/.rpm Linux packages, built via CPack and verified end to end in disposable containers, alongside the existing plain tarball.
Real README screenshots and a per-distro dependency list, with Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora, and Arch all directly verified against real builds.
A real preferences system (show-hidden-files toggle, default protocol, persisted window layout) plus three real UI bug fixes.
Both core protocols — SFTP and FTP/FTPS — now verified end to end against real, independently-implemented servers.
